Every perf median in tests/perf/customers-list.perf.test.ts (six sorts, segment counts, three searches at the 20,000-customer capacity seed) lands under the 150 ms budget, with the list's rows, segments, counts, cursor behavior and role-shaped money byte-identical to today.

references.purpose: The capacity contract: the seed shape (20k customers / 60k addresses / 30k agreements / 120k bills / 40k visits), the six sorts, counts and three searches, each with a 150 ms median budget; runs only in the Performance Baselines job (CI + BATCH_E_PERF).

The implementation this card changed: at Step 0 it read BASE_FROM over the view (the list query, the hydration query and the counts query all read it). As built: phased base-table queries — fetchOrderedIds (ids only), fetchFactsByIds (window facts), hydrateWindow (the role-gated laterals — next job, oldest open bill — kept for window rows only); segment counts keep one grouped-aggregate pass over FACTS_FROM.

references.purpose: The segment rules in two forms — JS predicates over view facts and SQL conditions over a view alias. The redesign re-expresses the SQL form over base tables; the JS form's fact set defines what the ids phase must compute.

references.purpose: Why the view is slow: per-customer LATERAL aggregates over agreements, bills and visits for every live customer before any filter, sort or limit can apply; also the indexes the CU-1 build already added for those laterals.

references.purpose: The named follow-up from AR-4c's close-out: the measured problem (~1.6 s / ~0.9 s against the 150 ms budget at the capacity seed) and the prescribed direction.

risk: The segment SQL and the sort orders are the contract surface: a subtle re-expression (NULL ordering on owed/rent, the attention sort's composite keys, search's phone-digits trigram path) can pass the small integration fixtures while diverging at capacity. Mitigation: S1 captures EXPLAIN ANALYZE and a row-level parity dump (ids per sort/segment at a mid-size seed) from the view implementation BEFORE touching it, and S2/S3 must reproduce that dump exactly from base tables.
sequence: S1 baseline + design: perf timings and EXPLAIN ANALYZE for the three view queries on a disposable 20k database; a parity dump (ordered ids per sort, per segment, counts, search hits) at a mid-size seed; the per-sort base-table design recorded in the slice commit

S2 getCustomerList two-phase: ids window per sort from base tables (segment SQL re-expressed in segments.ts), hydration laterals scoped to the window ids; parity dump reproduced; integration + segments + keys suites green
S3 counts + search: getCustomerSegmentCounts and the name/phone/address search paths on base tables; counts parity against the view on the same fixtures

S4 perf proof + PR: perf suite all medians < 150 ms on the disposable 20k database, packet checks, preflight, STATUS + AR-4 card updates; CI incl. customers-list browser spec and the Performance Baselines job
